title: Beat & Rhythm Skill (REVISED)
revision_note: Previously implied most notes lie on a beat and that an eighth-note is a minimum. Now beat grids are candidate hypotheses; syncopation, triplets, swing, pickups and rubato are explicitly preserved.
purpose: Understand tempo, beats, and note durations so the grid is used as a PRIOR, never as a deletion or forced-snapping rule.

tempo.definition: Speed of the beat in BPM. One beat = 60/BPM seconds.

common.110-140: Upbeat — lively, more notes per phrase

note_durations_at_bpm.formula: whole=4 beats, half=2, quarter=1, eighth=0.5, triplet=1/3, sixteenth=0.25 beats.
note_durations_at_bpm.example_120_bpm: beat=0.5s, half=1.0s, quarter=0.5s, eighth=0.25s, triplet=0.166s, sixteenth=0.125s.
note_durations_at_bpm.use: Compute the eighth/triplet/sixteenth durations to JUDGE durations — but short notes are legitimately present in runs, grace notes and ornamentation.

beat_and_grid.rule: The beat grid is a HYPOTHESIS. Many onsets are near a beat/subdivision, but syncopation, pickups, swing and rubato are musically valid off-grid placements.
beat_and_grid.action: Do NOT snap notes to the grid by default. Only adjust an onset when the onset confidence is low and the nearest grid point is strongly supported. Preserve genuine micro-timing/rubato.

rhythmic_devices.syncopation: Accents on weak beats or off-beats — musically valid, do not remove.
rhythmic_devices.pickup_notes: Anacrusis notes before the downbeat — valid, do not delete.
rhythmic_devices.triplets: Three equal notes in the space of two — valid, preserve their timing.
rhythmic_devices.swing: Consistent subtle off-beat offset — preserve as groove.

taal.definition: Hindustani rhythmic cycles: Teen Taal (16 beats), Keherwa (8), Dadra (6), Ek Taal (12), Jhaptaal (10).
taal.note: Tempo and phrase length may suggest a taal, but this is labeling only — it never justifies moving or deleting notes.
